To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we identified 266 copy number alterations probes that are significantly associated with adenocarcinomas and squamous cell carcinomas of non-small cell lung cancer.

we compared the genome- wide CNAs of 208 early-stage ACA and 93 SCC tumor samples, identified 266 CNA regions for distinguishing these two subtypes and revealed that the genes in the CNA regions were enriched in lung-cancer related pathways.

the genome-wide CNAs of early stage NSCLC are different in ACA and SCC and the genes corresponding to those different CNAs are enriched in lung cancer-related pathways and chromosome regions where CNO usually occur in lung cancers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the classification of NSCLC based on CNAs and the potential of CNAs as biomarkers for NSCLC.
the CNA of NSCLC, which is a valuable supplement to the current research of the genetic basis of lung cancer and will be of great help to the clinical diagnosis and treatment of NSCLC patients.
the genome-wide CNAs of NSCLC, which is helpful to the classification and prognosis of NSCLC.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CNA patterns can be utilized for the classification of NSCLC.
CNA is a promising biomarker for NSCLC classification.
the 266 CNA probe set is a good classifier for distinguishing ACA from SCC.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CNA patterns of early stage NSCLC are different from each other, especially between ACA and SCC.
CNA probes located at the chromosomal regions where CNA occurs in lung cancer are more valuable in distinguishing different subgroups in lung cancer than those at other chromosomal regions.
CNA probes in the chromosome regions of 1p, 3q, 5q, 8q, 9p, 11q, 13q and 17q are of great importance in the diagnosis of ACA and SCC.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the copy number alterations in the lung cancer genome are associated with the histopathological subtypes.
the CNA patterns are different in ACA and SCC and the genes that are associated with the 266 CNA probe regions are enriched in pathways related to lung cancer.
the genes corresponding with these 266 probes are enriched in lung cancer pathways, suggesting that these genes may play important role in the pathogenesis of NSCLC.
